prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Green Party’s 2019 manifesto is a call to act now, in dark days of Brexit turmoil and a broken democracy, to confront the climate and ecological emergency and deliver social justice. As the originators of the Green New Deal (GND), the Greens argue they are the only party you can trust to tackle the crisis at the necessary speed and scale while fixing deep social and economic inequalities. If not now, when?

Core mission: a ten‑year Green New Deal to reach net zero by 2030 and build a safer, fairer future
- Invest over £100bn a year (plus UBI) to transform energy, housing, transport, industry, and land use, creating millions of green jobs, restoring nature, and shifting the economy from GDP growth to wellbeing.
- Devolve power and resources, enable community and common ownership, and establish public banking to steer low-cost finance into the transition.
- Ensure a just transition: target investment to the places and people who need it most; work with trade unions so no one is left behind.
- Fund a Universal Basic Income so everyone has security to participate in the transition.

Green New Deal pillars
- Energy: massive renewables build-out (around 70% electricity from wind by 2030), grid and storage upgrades, community energy, end fossil subsidies, rising carbon tax to phase out coal, oil and gas, interconnectors to Europe; ban fracking; oppose new nuclear.
- Housing: insulate every home; deep retrofit 1m homes a year; 100,000 new Passivhaus‑standard council homes annually; heat pumps and local heat networks; EPC A for rentals; solar for 1m homes a year; planning that prioritises renovation and car‑free living.
- Transport: make public transport cheaper than driving; electrify rail and expand lines; reopen stations; bring rail into public ownership; bus franchising everywhere; £2.5bn/year for walking and cycling; no new runways or road capacity; frequent flyer levy; ban new petrol/diesel car sales by 2030; Vision Zero and 20 mph default.
- Industry: UK clean manufacturing renaissance; R&D and grants to decarbonise; regional mutual banks; right to repair and 10‑year warranties; cut single‑use plastics; near‑100% recycling; CCS for steel/cement; just transition from North Sea oil.
- Food, farming & forestry: 10‑year shift to agroecology; major pesticide cuts; GM moratorium; 700m trees; rewilding; hedgerow restoration; urban food growing; right to food; flood prevention through nature; Land Commission and LVT; support “less but better” meat with a phased levy recycled to farmers.

Income security: Universal Basic Income
- Phase in UBI so no one is worse off: adults £89/week; pensioners £178/week; supplements for children, disability, carers and lone parents; Housing Benefit retained where needed; partly funded by carbon tax.

Four enabling programmes
- Say Yes to Europe: a People’s Vote with Remain; transform the EU for democracy, social rights and climate leadership; defend freedom of movement; humane refugee policy.
- Grow Democracy: proportional representation for all elections; fully elected second chamber; votes at 16; citizens’ assemblies and a People’s Constitution; protect media pluralism; Digital Bill of Rights; powerful devolution; new Carbon Chancellor and Future Generations Act; scrap the Home Office in favour of a Ministry for Sanctuary; reorient defence to peace and climate security.
- Green Quality of Life Guarantee: end austerity; sustained NHS investment and de‑privatisation; free social care at home for over‑65s; restore and transform education (funding boost, end high‑stakes testing/Ofsted, free childcare 35 hours from 9 months, scrap tuition fees and write off debt); stronger workers’ rights (Living Wage £12, gig‑economy protections, 10:1 pay ratio); rent controls and end no‑fault evictions; move toward a shorter working week.
- New Deal for Tax and Spend: simplify taxes into a Consolidated Income Tax; tax wealth like work; raise Corporation Tax to 24%; clamp down on avoidance and tax havens; replace Council Tax and Business Rates with a fair Land Value Tax; end wasteful projects (Trident, HS2, road‑building, airport expansion) to fund the GND.

Further commitments
- Restore nature (ecocide law, clean air/soil, right to roam, marine protection) and transform animal welfare (ban hunting and live exports; end badger cull; phase out animal testing).
- End the war on drugs with a regulated, health‑first approach; expand restorative justice and halve the prison population.
- Global justice: increase aid to 1% GNI, climate‑proof development, fair trade rules, and an international ecocide law.

Paying for it
- Around £141.5bn/year current spending funded by tax reform and savings; £94.4bn/year capital borrowing for GND investment; crowd in ~£50bn/year private co‑investment; carbon tax revenue transitions as emissions fall, replaced by returns from a fairer, greener economy.

Every Green vote is a vote to put climate justice, democracy, and wellbeing first—and to begin the transformation now.
